inventory.description: Pure, host-testable products of Packages/VisualCore: VisualCoreMath, VisualCoreSimulation, VisualCoreScenes, VisualCoreShaderSource, VisualCoreEffectsGraph, VisualCoreDiagnostics, VisualCoreAudioDSP, VisualCorePersistence, VisualCoreParameters, VisualCoreExperience (+ VisualCoreTestSupport for test targets). iOS products of Packages/VisualCoreRendering: VisualCoreRendering, VisualCoreEffects, VisualCoreUI, VisualCoreAudio (links AVFAudio), VisualCoreAutomation, VisualCoreExperienceHost. For the arcade (checked 2026-11-14): VisualCoreSimulation has SeededRandom, FixedStepClock, FixedStepRunner (FixedStepSimulation, ControlStream), ParticleSystem with Emitter and EmitterBurst, Tween and Timeline, HapticPlanner, AnnouncementPlanner and transitionDuration (AccessibilityPlans.swift); VisualCoreScenes has the 2D SceneNode tree with Primitive rect, circle, line, polygon and polyline, Primitive.contains (point in shape) and SceneNode.hitTest, PointerTracker, PointerVelocityTracker, the tap and drag recognizers and GestureArbiter; VisualCoreRendering has PrimitiveRenderer and ParticleRenderer; VisualCoreEffects has the bloom pass; VisualCoreExperienceHost has ExperienceFeedback (haptics switch and announcements). No 2D shape-against-shape overlap and no swept or continuous collision test exists in any framework product (the 'intersect' matches are mesh and camera-bound helpers); VisualCoreAudio holds input sources only (demo, file, microphone, test signal), no sound playback (grep 2026-11-14).

RenderHost (@MainActor) owns the EGL display, context and surfaces over ANGLE's Metal backend (EGLDisplayProvider), the CAMetalLayer RenderView, the FrameScheduler and context generations; pause/resume, replaceScene, recreateContext, renderOffscreen and destroy; scenes implement RenderScene setup/resize/render/teardown. All EGL and GL work runs on the main thread. Neon Arcade's fixed-step game loop (player, hazards, orbs, collision, scoring) is GPU-free CPU work stepped on the main thread at the frame boundary; drawing reads finished state and never changes it. Neon Arcade adds no EGL or GL context of its own.

ResourceRegistry creates buffers, textures, programs and render targets under a ResourceBudget and rejects stale handles after a generation change. ShaderProgram, ShaderBundle and ShaderLibrary (#include expansion with line maps) compile bundled GLSL; the vc/ library holds color, field, hash, noise, palette and sdf helpers. PrimitiveRenderer draws a 2D SceneNode tree as one batched triangle list through Camera2D; ParticleRenderer draws particle instances in one batch; FullScreenShaderScene and the effects graph (copy, colorMatrix, blur, bloom, distort, composite, feedback, flashLimit; EffectScene, EffectRenderer) give the glow.

ExperienceSession opens, checkpoints, closes and recovers an Experience on one RenderHost, applies the quality level (QualityGovernor over the experience's QualityProfile, fed by DeviceConditions thermal state and Low Power Mode) and memory/scene-phase events; ExperienceShell adapts an ExperiencePresenter (scene, controls) to Experience; ExperienceCore is the GPU-free state with its qualityTiers; ExperienceStorage is the per-experience sandbox; ExperienceFeedback routes haptics (behind the app's haptics switch) and announcements; the one app registers experiences in ExperienceRegistry and Catalog/registrations.json (nine registered, A01-A09; Neon Arcade joins in A10-P01 and stays unregistered and unavailable in A10-P00; scripts/check_experience_packages.py forbids unregistered targets). Neon Arcade needs no microphone, camera, photos or location; sounds are synthesized, not recorded, so no usage description or privacy answer changes.

XcodeGen spec project.yml for the one app (target VisualCore), package schemes via scripts/xcodebuild_package.py, app tests via scripts/xcodebuild_app.py, and scripts/release_check.py: 103 named steps listed by --list on 2026-11-14 (shared checks, package and app builds/tests, per-experience release, copy-claims and verify steps of A01-A09 on iOS 27 and 26, release audits of the one app, the seven reference regression steps).

Neon Arcade owns its domain (Neon Dodge's lanes, player, hazards, orbs, waves, difficulty, lives and scoring, input replay, title/pause/game-over flow, steering sensitivity, local high scores, glow readability caps, synthesized sound choices, the spoken game-state description and content licenses) and UI under Packages/ExperiencesCreative/NeonArcade/ (Core GPU-free, CoreTests, Experience with Adapter/, ExperienceTests, Shaders, scenario-manifest.json; created in A10-P01, not present today). VisualCore owns reusable machinery: the seeded fixed-step clock and runner, particles and the 2D collision to come (circle and capsule overlap, swept tests; VisualCoreSimulation), 2D shapes and gestures (VisualCoreScenes, drawn by VisualCoreRendering), bloom and flash limiting (VisualCoreEffects), synthesized sound-effect playback to come (VisualCoreAudio), quality, persistence and storage (constitution Principle II, A10 section). ProjectM stays in the harness.

Reference pinned at d93edd1, read-only; scripts/run_reference_baseline.py lists the ordered reference steps; scripts/check_reference_clean.py checks the submodule; the 7 release-check steps run in two chunks via release_check.py --only (reference-engine-xcframework, reference-build-projectm-ios-sim, reference-clean; reference-test-anglerendering-ios27, reference-test-anglerendering-ios26, projectm-reference-ios27, projectm-reference-ios26), recorded in docs/apps/neon-arcade/regression-baseline.md.

FixedStepClock (default 1/120 s, at most 8 steps per frame, interpolation alpha) and FixedStepRunner over a FixedStepSimulation with a ControlStream of timed commands give deterministic, frame-rate-independent stepping (the base for input replay); SeededRandom (SplitMix64) and SeedDerivation give reproducible streams; StateDigest fingerprints state; ParticleSystem steps seeded emitters with a bounded capacity. Particle Universe (A04) and Digital Aquarium (A09) step this way; Neon Dodge's rules will too, so the same seed and inputs give the same outcome.

matrix.capability: 2D rendering: player, hazards, orbs, lanes and backgrounds as SceneNode shapes (circle, rect, line, polygon, polyline) with transform, z order, visibility and colour, batched into one triangle list per tree through Camera2D on the main thread
matrix.source: brainstorm: 2D rendering; manual risk draw overhead
matrix.notes: Tested in VisualCoreScenesTests/SceneGraphTests, VisualCoreRenderingTests/PrimitiveRendererTests and VisualCoreMathTests. Draw overhead: every node of a tree lands in one batch (one draw); polygons are capped at 256 points and polylines at 8,192; the audit does not measure performance (spec edge case). Shapes are procedural, never bitmap art.

gaps.justification: Found in A10-P00: no shape-against-shape overlap and no swept test exists in any framework product; circle and capsule overlap and swept tests are generic 2D game machinery and belong to VisualCoreSimulation (clarification 5). The swept case is proved by A10-P03's fast-hazard fixture.
gaps.test: Host tests (Collision2DTests, 13 tests): circle-circle and circle-capsule overlap agree with analytic answers including touching, inside, both rounded ends and a degenerate segment; the swept circle-circle test returns 0 when already touching, the analytic earliest fraction in [0, 1] for crossings and nil for misses, and catches tunnelling at 4, 10 and 50 times the summed radii per step; NaN/Inf and negative radii give no hit; deterministic (API baseline additive). Capsules are not swept: their fall speed is bounded below the summed radii per step (GameSimulationTests). A10-P03 fixture (HighSpeedFixtureTests): circle hazards at 20, 50 and 100 units/s crossing the player within one step are hit, and the same 1.5 units to the side are not.

gaps.justification: Neon Dodge's rules (lanes, player, hazards, orbs, waves, difficulty, lives, scoring), the input replay format and the content license fields are the game's domain over VisualCore's fixed-step runner, ControlStream, SeededRandom and the 2D collision of G-COLLISION2D (clarification 5). Phase 01 part built in A10-P01: GameRun, GameSimulation (fixed step, spawning, swept collision, scoring, lives, replayable inputs), ArcadeCatalog and LicenseAudit (content licenses); lanes, waves and difficulty remain for A10-P02.
gaps.test: Host tests (swift test, no GPU): the same seed and input replay give the same state digest; hits cost a life, orbs score once, waves and difficulty follow their tables within caps on hazards and orbs; drawing never changes the state; every palette, pattern and shader records an author and a license and the audit fails on a missing one. Lanes and full mechanics complete in A10-P02

gaps.justification: Found in A10-P00: VisualCoreAudio holds input sources only (demo, file, microphone, test signal); synthesized sound-effect playback (short code-generated tones, no recordings) is generic and belongs to VisualCoreAudio (clarification 5).
gaps.test: Host tests: synthesized effects render deterministic, bounded, click-free buffers (no NaN, peak below full scale, fade in and out); simulator tests: playback starts and stops without a microphone permission, respects the sound switch and silences on interruption and background

gaps.justification: The title, playing, paused and game-over screens and their transitions are the game's flow over the presenter, PlaybackState, Tween and transitionDuration; no generic transition component is needed beyond the experience lifecycle states.
gaps.test: Host tests: the flow allows only title -> playing -> paused/game over -> restart, pause stops the fixed-step loop and background never fast-forwards, restart starts from a fresh seed, and transitions take 0 s under Reduce Motion

gaps.justification: Mapping drag translation to lane or horizontal position with a person-chosen sensitivity is game-specific; it is built over DragRecognizer and GestureArbiter, with native controls as the alternative.
gaps.test: Host tests: each sensitivity step maps a drag to a bounded movement, the setting persists, the native buttons reach the same positions (GestureAlternatives.missing is empty), and steering is recorded as replayable commands

gaps.justification: The local high-score table is the game's document stored crash-safe in ExperienceStorage through VisualCorePersistence; no online leaderboard.
gaps.test: Host tests: scores round-trip, a write interrupted mid-way keeps the previous table, damaged or newer files are reported and never crash, the table keeps a bounded number of entries in order

gaps.justification: Readability caps (bloom intensity and radius, particle counts, brightness and glow pulses per quality tier) are the game's policy over the shared bloom pass, particle budget and flash limiter.
gaps.test: Host tests: per tier the bloom parameters, particle counts and brightness stay within the stated caps, Reduce Flashing removes glow pulses; simulator tests: hazards, player and score keep a minimum contrast against the glow

reasons: A working host and drawing path exist: RenderHost on OpenGL ES -> ANGLE -> Metal, PrimitiveRenderer drawing a SceneNode tree in one batch through Camera2D, ParticleRenderer and the bloom pass, all public and tested.
8 of 17 rows are available with tests: 2D rendering, particles, animation, input handling, persistence, quality tiers and low power, accessibility and Reduce Motion, lifecycle.

All gaps are additive and owned: G-COLLISION2D (circle and capsule overlap, swept tests; VisualCoreSimulation, upstream) in A10-P01 with the swept case proved by A10-P03's fixture; G-SOUNDFX (synthesized sound-effect playback; VisualCoreAudio, upstream) in A10-P03; app-local G-GAMERULES (rules, input replay, lanes, content licenses) in A10-P01/P02, G-TRANSITIONS in A10-P03, G-STEERINPUT and G-HIGHSCORES in A10-P04, G-GLOWCAPS in A10-P05.

No permission and no privacy answer changes; Neon Arcade stays unregistered until A10-P01 creates Packages/ExperiencesCreative/NeonArcade with its targets and first real rules, so the experience package check and the one app are unchanged.
